Title: Andante appassionato
Notes: A slow section Dvořák cut from String Quartet No. 6 when he revised it (probably 1874); it begins in a minor, and Burghauser supplied an F major ending so it can be played on its own.

Title: Quartet Movement
Notes: Quartet Movement in F major: the finished first movement of a quartet for the Hellmesberger Quartet that Dvořák abandoned in October 1881 to write No. 11 instead; first performed on Czech Radio in 1945.

Title: Cypresses
Notes: Twelve of his 1865 Cypresses songs arranged for string quartet in 1887 under the title Echo of Songs; published in 1921 in an edition by Josef Suk, who gave it the name Cypresses.

Title: Two Waltzes
Notes: Two Waltzes: Dvořák's own arrangement of Nos. 1 and 4 of his piano Waltzes, Op. 54, for string quartet (or string orchestra), with No. 4 moved from D-flat to D major; published in 1911.

Title: Andante (fragment)
Notes: a 29-bar Andante fragment, dated summer 1812(?) and perhaps a rejected slow movement for D 32, that breaks off and is not performable without completion.

Title: Overture
Notes: a complete single-movement overture, Schubert's own string-quartet arrangement (after 12 July 1811) of his overture for string quintet D 8, first published by Peters in 1970.

Title: Minuet
Notes: a single complete 37-bar minuet for string quartet, probably from November 1813.

Title: Five Minuets and Five German Dances
Notes: five minuets with six trios and five German dances with seven trios and a coda, dated 19 November 1813; the German dances were formerly catalogued separately as D 90.

Title: Quartet Movement
Notes: an opening movement dated 23 April 1814 whose autograph breaks off after 296 bars, at the recapitulation; Alfred Orel's performing completion was published in 1939.
